$comment: Machine-readable so your migration runner can enumerate these instead of a
human transcribing SQL out of a Markdown file. Nothing here applies
anything: `MIGRATIONS.md` section 2's position is unchanged, which is that
`version` is the entry number in MIGRATIONS.md. Entries 1 and 2 predate the
oldest tag in the repository, so there is no previous schema to apply them
to and no way to verify them; they have no file. Entries 4, 7 and 9 changed
no schema. The gaps are the entries that cost you nothing.

migrations.title: a password is refused where it was never enforced
migrations.decision: This file REVOKES grants whose password never protected anything, which is the recommended answer. The alternative -- keep them readable, drop the inert hash -- is commented at the bottom of the file. MIGRATIONS.md Entry 3 presents both as consecutive statements; running that block does both.

migrations.title: every index on file_grant becomes reachable
migrations.note: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY and DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction. A runner that wraps each file in one must not wrap this.

migrations.title: TRUNCATE on the audit log is refused
migrations.note: Entry 6's REVOKE block is a privilege recommendation with a placeholder, not part of this file. Do it anyway, in your own grants management.

migrations.title: two columns, an index and a constraint, for pre-authorized upload
migrations.note: Nullable columns with no default, so no table rewrite and no backfill. CONCURRENTLY and NOT VALID + VALIDATE throughout, which is correct on an empty table as well as a large one.

migrations.title: the schema version table
migrations.note: Only for a database created before 0.15.0. schema.sql creates and stamps this table itself.

migrations.title: audit retention: checkpoints, a trimmable chain, and a deletable tenant

unverifiable.why: predates the oldest tag (v0.4.4), so there is no previous schema to apply it to. Entry 1 is also not a complete script: it ends by telling you to copy three blocks verbatim from the 0.3.0 schema.sql, which the tree no longer contains.
